pointers.sentence: Two changes of 6.1 alter how the admin works: an action is an `Action` whose locations can offer it on a change form as well as on the change list; and a change list joins the foreign keys its columns name, not every non-null one, a gain, the notes say, for models with many foreign keys (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

Since 6.1 each value is an `Action`, which adds a plural description and the **locations**, members of `ActionLocation`: `ActionLocation.CHANGE_LIST`, the default, and `ActionLocation.CHANGE_FORM`, a change page's one object (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:Action`).

The decorator `django.contrib.admin.action` takes `location=`, one location or a list, and `description_plural=`, the change list's text in place of `description=` (`django/contrib/admin/decorators.py:action`; [Actions: `response_action` and `delete_selected`](../admin/actions.md)).

The old shapes warn since 6.1, and work until Django 2028: an `Action` unpacked or indexed gives the tuple's members (`Action.__iter__`), and an override of `get_actions` or `ModelAdmin.get_action_choices` without `action_location=` is found by its signature and called without it on the change list (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._get_actions_with_action_location`).

With `ModelAdmin.list_select_related` false, the default, a change list showing a foreign key used to call `select_related()` with no fields, which follows every foreign key that cannot be null (`django/db/models/query_utils.py:select_related_descend`): "all foreign key fields", the 6.1 notes say (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

With `ModelAdmin.list_select_related` false, the default, a change list showing a foreign key used to call `select_related()` with no fields, which follows every foreign key that cannot be null (`django/db/models/query_utils.py:select_related_descend`): "all foreign key fields", the 6.1 notes say (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

Since 6.1 only the keys that columns name are joined, as `ChangeList.get_select_related_fields`, which replaced has_related_field_in_list_display, collects them (`django/contrib/admin/views/main.py:ChangeList.get_select_related_fields`; [The change list: `changelist_view` and `ChangeList`](../admin/change-list.md)).

None of the four releases joins a key for a column passing through it, as "author__name" passes through author: unless something else joins it, each row's author is fetched by a query of its own, under the default fetch mode since 6.1, the choice of what such a read does (`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py:ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.__get__`; [Deferred fields and fetch modes in a queryset](../querysets/deferred.md)).
A class that sets it warns as it is defined, asking for `False` or the fields to fetch (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.__init_subclass__`).

5.0 gave it the request as a third argument, which `ChangeList.get_filters` passes by position (`django/contrib/admin/views/main.py:ChangeList.get_filters`); 5.0 deprecated overrides without it, and 6.0 dropped the fallback that called them with two.

Since 6.1 a column of `ModelAdmin.list_display` that crosses a relation and ends at a boolean field, such as "author__active", is drawn as the boolean icon (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_list.py:items_for_result`).

At this commit every log method of `ModelAdmin` writes through `log_actions`, which saves a single entry with `Model.save` and several with one `QuerySet.bulk_create` (`django/contrib/admin/models.py:LogEntryManager.log_actions`; [The log and the history: `LogEntry` and `history_view`](../admin/log.md)).

Since 6.0 an override of log_deletion, or of a manager's log_action, is not called, and nothing warns; `log_actions` writes the entries without it (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.log_deletions`).

`ModelAdmin.history_view` loads the object first, and since 6.2 refuses a user without the view or change permission, with `PermissionDenied`, a 403, before it answers that the object is missing (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.history_view`).

"View on site" has been the site's own view since 6.2, `AdminSite.shortcut_view`, which raises `PermissionDenied` when the model is registered and its model admin's `BaseModelAdmin.has_view_permission` is false (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.shortcut_view`; [The site's own pages: the index, the login and `AdminSite.each_context`](../admin/site-views.md)).
